sections.heading: 2. Price bounded obligations and allocate ownership explicitly
paragraphs: Use a master services agreement for recurring commercial terms and a statement of work for each bounded sprint. The statement should name inputs, connectors, output formats, volume limits, supported environments, acceptance tests, and exclusions. Replace 'automate customer support' with 'classify up to 2,000 monthly tickets into twelve agreed categories, draft responses, and route every draft to a client reviewer.' Define a measurable quality test using a client-approved evaluation set, including ambiguous examples and prohibited disclosures. Specify that changes to categories, source systems, languages, or autonomous actions require a priced change order. A fee trigger can be 50% at booking, 30% when the sandbox passes named tests, and 20% at production handoff; payment milestones and accounting recognition are separate questions. Give the client a defined acceptance window and a written method for identifying reproducible defects. Do not make silence waive hidden security defects or mandatory statutory rights. Support terms must distinguish response time from restoration time and identify excluded third-party outages. Document client dependencies, especially credential delivery and reviewer availability, so their delay moves the schedule rather than creating unpaid standby work.

Allocate intellectual property by category rather than writing 'client owns everything.' List preexisting agency libraries, reusable templates, client-specific configuration, client source data, third-party components, and generated outputs separately. Under 17 U.S.C. § 204(a), transfers of copyright ownership generally require a signed writing; contractor work should not be assumed to qualify automatically as work made for hire. Obtain contractor assignments where appropriate and give the client a durable license to embedded reusable components. Do not promise exclusive copyright in purely machine-generated material or rights the model provider cannot convey. Data terms should prohibit using client records to train unrelated products without a separate, specific agreement. Address subprocessors, export formats, deletion, and transition support at termination. Negotiate a liability cap tied to a defined fee period, with express treatment of confidentiality, intellectual-property claims, fraud, and liabilities that applicable law will not allow parties to limit. A dispute clause should identify governing law, forum, escalation timing, and whether arbitration applies. Narrow any anti-circumvention term to identified introductions and deliberate fee avoidance; exclude preexisting relationships and independent inbound contacts instead of claiming ownership over the client's entire market.

Keep scenario economics tied to implementation fees and support retainers. An illustrative Conservative mix is ten $6,000 sprints plus five $8,000 annual support packages: $60,000 + $40,000 = $100,000 revenue. At 20% net margin, annual costs total $80,000 and owner profit equals $20,000. Base can comprise twenty-five $14,000 sprints plus ten $20,000 annual retainers: $350,000 + $200,000 = $550,000 revenue, with $385,000 costs and $165,000 owner profit at 30.0%. Scaled can comprise forty $15,000 sprints plus twenty $20,000 annual retainers: $600,000 + $400,000 = $1,000,000 revenue, with $600,000 costs and $400,000 owner profit at 40%. The canonical teams remain 2 FT + 3 C for Conservative and Base, and 3 FT + 4 C for Scaled. Contractor counts describe roster size, not automatically full-time commitments. These are annualized illustrations, not evidence that five market-rate salaries fit the Conservative budget. Reconcile actual compensation, API charges, insurance, acquisition, rework, and support against the cost envelope before hiring. Client sales influenced by automation, carrier settlement receipts, and customer transaction principal never become agency revenue merely because the agency dashboard displays them.

sections.heading: 3. Turn reputation monitoring into a defensible service, not suppression
paragraphs: The mapped play review_gating_reputation_extortion_funnels requires a firm redesign around legitimate monitoring. For medspas, dental implant practices, roofers, and auto dealers, monitor new one-star reviews on Google Business Profiles, Trustpilot, and Yelp only through permitted interfaces, licensed feeds, or authorized manual review. Do not evade rate limits or assume public visibility creates permission for unrestricted extraction. Offer timestamped alerts, review-velocity reporting, response drafts, and evidence-based platform-policy assessments. An alert within minutes is a measured service objective only where the authorized feed supports that latency; otherwise state the actual polling interval. The Federal Trade Commission Act, 15 U.S.C. § 45, prohibits deceptive practices, while 16 CFR Part 465 addresses fake reviews, specified incentive practices, and review suppression. Never condition a refund, service recovery, or payment on removing an honest negative review. Never threaten exposure, fabricate policy violations, or claim a special platform relationship. The Consumer Review Fairness Act, 15 U.S.C. § 45b, also restricts covered form-contract terms that prohibit or penalize honest consumer reviews. A B2B agency contract should require client cooperation with these operating boundaries rather than quietly funding prohibited tactics.

Apply the fallback precisely: provide equal post-service review invitations to all eligible customers, without filtering by satisfaction, and flag only genuine platform-policy-violating spam or other documented violations. Equal treatment alone is insufficient if the solicitation violates the destination platform's rules. Google prohibits incentivized reviews, and Yelp discourages businesses from soliciting reviews; use a neutral private-feedback channel where direct solicitation is unsuitable. Recheck current platform rules before activating each destination. A Google invitation can read: 'Thank you for choosing our team. If you would like to share your experience, you can leave an honest review using the review link in this message. Positive, mixed, and critical feedback are equally welcome. Participation is optional and does not affect your service.' The system supplies the verified business link and uses an authorized communication channel. Do not send happy customers to a public review page while diverting unhappy customers into a private form. For a disputed review, preserve the original text, URL, timestamp, policy provision, and supporting evidence. Request platform review without promising removal. A healthcare response should invite private contact without confirming patient status or discussing treatment details.

Make the unit economics support patient, evidence-led work rather than coercive urgency. An illustrative $500 monthly monitoring package across twenty locations produces $10,000 monthly service billings, or $120,000 annualized if retained for twelve months. Budget $80 per location for authorized data and messaging, $100 for human review, and $70 for account operations: $250 direct cost per location and $5,000 monthly contribution before acquisition and shared overhead. This is an optional service-line illustration inside an agency portfolio, not an addition to the canonical scorecard or an owner-profit forecast. At sixty alerts monthly and twelve minutes of review per alert, the team needs twelve reviewer hours before escalations. If volume doubles, the contract must specify additional capacity pricing or a revised response target. The fallback is a lower-frequency monitoring and neutral-feedback service, not automated mass reporting. Measure alert latency, evidence quality, response turnaround, and client retention. Do not sell predicted star-rating increases or recovered sales without defensible measurement. For any performance claim, retain the baseline, measurement window, sample size, exclusions, and attribution limits. Never classify every negative reviewer as a competitor or every removed review as proof of agency-created revenue.

sections.heading: 4. Screen telecom economics and use evidence-based outreach scripts
paragraphs: The mapped play telecom_voice_traffic_pumping_8yy_sms_arbitrage describes revenue-sharing CLECs, international Tier-2/3 switches, free conference bridges, AI voice lines, radio call-in utilities, and OTP or A2P endpoints generating very large termination volumes. Treat that description as a high-risk screening case, not an implementation recipe. FCC access-stimulation rules include 47 CFR § 61.3(bbb) and § 51.914; ordinary customer demand does not automatically exempt a revenue-sharing arrangement. Require the carrier to identify the applicable service classification, settlement basis, access-stimulation analysis, and responsible contracting entities. An agency supplying software should not casually become the telecommunications provider of record. Depending on the actual service, federal authorizations, state public-utility obligations, registration, contributions, and other carrier duties may apply. Toll-free and messaging economics require separate analysis; voice attestation cannot validate SMS consent. Do not build artificial call generation, OTP abuse, or routing intended to obscure responsibility. The suggested fallback of distributing traffic across jurisdictions does not cure an unlawful arrangement. Replace it with a genuine user-requested utility funded by transparent subscriptions or documented service fees, using providers authorized for the actual routes and retaining attributable demand records.

Use simple economics to expose dependence on questionable settlements. At 20 million voice minutes monthly and an assumed $0.002 net settlement spread, the headline contribution is $40,000 before disputes, transport, fraud losses, and operating costs. A $0.002 change eliminates that entire spread. Those receipts belong to the relevant telecom operator, not automatically to the implementation agency. A safer illustrative agency engagement charges $12,000 for a bounded utility deployment plus $1,500 monthly support, producing $30,000 first-year fees over twelve support months. At $8,000 implementation cost and $800 monthly support cost, direct costs are $17,600 and contribution is $12,400 before shared overhead. Keep that illustration inside the canonical portfolio totals. Require genuine human initiation for the utility and verified caller identity where applicable. STIR/SHAKEN under 47 CFR § 64.6301 addresses caller-ID authentication duties for covered voice providers; it does not prove consent, lawful content, or lawful compensation. Use provider-documented attestation handling rather than inventing an agency certification. If carrier economics fail, retain the customer's legitimate workflow through subscription billing and ordinary metered transport, or discontinue the uneconomic feature. Never repair margin by manufacturing traffic or bypassing provider controls.

Keep outbound acquisition separate from deployed client messaging. Commercial email, including B2B outreach, is subject to CAN-SPAM, 15 U.S.C. § 7704: use accurate headers and subjects, applicable advertising identification, a valid physical postal address, and a working opt-out. Honor opt-outs within ten business days and supervise contractors sending on the agency's behalf. The scripts below are message bodies; production email must append the agency's verified postal address and functioning unsubscribe mechanism. Do not invent an address to make a template look complete. Before calls or texts, classify the technology, number type, purpose, recipient location, and applicable consent requirements under 47 U.S.C. § 227 and 47 CFR § 64.1200, alongside state restrictions. A published business number is not blanket permission for an AI-voice campaign. Artificial or prerecorded voice rules can apply independently of whether a system is an automatic telephone dialing system. Log the precise consent language, number, timestamp, source, and revocation status when consent is required. A discovery conversation should establish authority, baseline workload, permitted data, and measurable acceptance before discussing savings. Use named deliverables and observed facts instead of invented urgency, removal promises, or carrier-income claims the agency cannot substantiate.

sections.heading: 1. Turn the fixed-scope sprint into a measured automation system
paragraphs: Start with a product boundary that the five-person team can defend: one intake source, one bounded transformation, one destination, and one measurable acceptance test per sprint. The delivery lead owns architecture and client acceptance; the operations lead owns intake, support, and account economics. Three contractors cover integration engineering, test execution, and domain review through explicit work packets rather than standing attendance requirements. Sell additional destinations, historical migrations, and new decision classes as separately priced changes. In the statement of work, name authorized systems, permitted data fields, service accounts, retention periods, model providers, output ownership, and incident contacts. Access must come from the client resource owner, not from instructions embedded in uploaded documents. Treat 18 U.S.C. 1030 as a concrete reason to record access authorization and stop when that authorization expires. Build an inventory of every credential and external publication surface before connecting production. The deliverable is a repeatable workflow with an observable result, not a promise that an agent will navigate arbitrary business exceptions. A new client should require configuration and acceptance fixtures, while genuinely new business logic receives its own estimate and delivery window.

Measure automation against labor-weighted repetitive work, not the number of boxes colored green in a workflow editor. Suppose the baseline contains 1,000 monthly repetitive hours: 200 in research, 150 in qualification, 450 in fulfillment, and 200 in distribution operations. A designed workflow leaves 50, 45, 100, and 55 hours respectively, or 250 hours altogether. That removes 750 hours and achieves 75% automation of the defined baseline. If the new system also creates 80 hours of review and incident handling, remaining total effort is 330 hours and net labor reduction is 67%, not 75%. Both figures belong on the client dashboard, together with volume, error severity, and sampling coverage. Do not describe the illustrative 1,000 hours as the agency team's available capacity; it can represent work distributed across client organizations. Instrument each task with start time, completion time, reviewer minutes, rework cause, and a stable workflow version. Compare like cohorts before claiming savings. Randomly inspect apparently successful runs because exception-only sampling misses silent errors. Freeze the denominator for a reporting period so changing task definitions cannot manufacture an improvement that the customer's staff never experience.

Implement intake as a small Python HTTP service behind a managed TLS endpoint. Verify the provider's webhook signature against raw request bytes with hmac.compare_digest, validate timestamps, and reject replayed event identifiers. A successful response means durable receipt, not completed business work: persist the event and an outbox record atomically, then let workers deliver outbox messages to Amazon SQS. Use a unique constraint on tenant, source, and event identifier to collapse duplicates. Validate JSON field types, payload size, allowed destinations, and client entitlements before any model call. The LLM receives only the minimum necessary fields and returns a typed proposal with evidence references; deterministic Python validates the proposal before a separate executor considers side effects. Customer text is data, never authority to expand tool access. Keep secrets outside prompts and retrieve them through scoped service identities. Attach tenant identity at ingestion and enforce it again when reading evidence, writing outputs, and opening review queues. A dedicated client pause switch must stop new external actions without destroying queued evidence. This separation lets operators repair a connector without asking the model to improvise a recovery procedure inside a live account.

sections.heading: 2. Productize marketplace intelligence without manufacturing enforcement claims
paragraphs: Use amazon_asin_hijack_brand_protection_trigger as a narrowly defined intelligence-and-case-preparation service, not an automatic accusation engine. Monitor Amazon, Walmart, and eBay offers through authorized marketplace APIs, licensed feeds, or expressly permitted collection methods. Buy Box and comparable winning-offer data availability varies by marketplace and account permission; unsupported fields must remain outside the contracted coverage. Capture product identifier, seller identity as represented by the platform, offer price, shipping charge, observation time, source reference, and collection method. Normalize comparable pack sizes before flagging undercutting. For 1,000 products observed four times daily across three marketplaces, the planning ceiling is 12,000 observations daily and 360,000 in a thirty-day month. At an illustrative licensed-feed cost of $0.002 per observation, acquisition costs $720 monthly before storage, review, and support. Confirm actual provider pricing and permitted refresh frequency before quoting. Deduplicate repeated offers into seller-product episodes rather than billing the reviewer for identical alerts. An observed lower price establishes a monitoring event; it does not establish counterfeiting, lost sales, or a legally actionable breach. Preserve that distinction in both the database schema and the customer-facing dossier.

Build each dossier from evidence rather than persuasive model narration. Python joins observations to the client's authorized reseller roster, written distribution terms, lot records, and documented warranty conditions. The LLM summarizes the timeline and identifies missing evidence without deciding that a seller is unlawful. A human checks identity matching, product equivalence, policy applicability, and the proposed next action. A price difference of $12 across 200 offers indicates a $2,400 price-gap exposure calculation only if each offer represents one comparable unit; it is not realized revenue loss. Actual loss analysis needs transaction counts, attribution assumptions, and counterfactual evidence. Structure the lawful fallback around unilateral MAP policies where appropriate, documented warranty or packaging material differences, and supply-chain lot serialization. Under 15 U.S.C. 1, avoid facilitating agreements among competing resellers about prices, and evaluate applicable state restrictions separately. Trademark analysis under 15 U.S.C. 1114 and 1125 requires facts supporting the asserted claim; an unauthorized reseller label alone is insufficient. Never manufacture IP complaints. Route ambiguous cases to the brand's designated decision maker, suspend unsupported allegations, and retain the evidence supporting any authorized communication.

Package the commercial offer around monitoring coverage, review capacity, and response preparation. The mapped play's $2,500–$7,500 monthly enforcement-retainer range becomes an agency implementation and managed-support offer only when the contract specifies what the agency actually performs. At $5,000 monthly, one client produces $60,000 annual agency revenue; five full-year clients produce $300,000. That is the Base scenario's retainer component, not additional revenue layered over it. For an illustrative account, combine $720 data acquisition, eight reviewer hours at $60 for $480, and $300 of hosting and support allocation: $1,500 direct monthly cost leaves $3,500 before sales, management, and other shared expenses. Do not call that contribution owner profit. Create distribution through permissioned, redacted before-and-after dossiers, agency partnerships, and technical pages explaining evidence requirements for specific marketplaces. A referral request belongs after the client accepts a useful case outcome, not after every alert. Offer a bounded diagnostic using the prospect's supplied product list, then convert repeatable monitoring needs into a fixed-scope sprint. If source access disappears, reduce coverage explicitly, credit no invented observations, and offer client-supplied exports as the operational fallback until authorized collection resumes.

sections.heading: 3. Bound payment orchestration to approved merchants, routes, and responsibilities
paragraphs: Treat high_risk_payfac_iso_mid_cascading_arbitrage as a demanding integration pattern, not permission to bypass underwriting. Its wholesale ISO and orchestration concept spans 25–60 domestic and offshore acquiring banks and high-risk merchant categories, including telehealth GLP-1s or peptides, nutra subscriptions, sweepstakes gaming, high-ticket coaching, and AI companions. Those labels establish neither legality nor processor eligibility. A category rejected by one provider may be accepted only by another provider that knowingly approves the actual business, geography, products, fulfillment, and descriptor. The productized agency should sell implementation and monitoring to authorized payment operators unless it separately holds the contracts and responsibilities required for another role. Collect each acquirer's written merchant approval, permitted transaction types, retry rules, settlement currency, and designated incident contact. Maintain a route registry that workers can read but an LLM cannot modify. New merchant identifiers require verified ownership and approved routing configuration. Offshore connectivity does not remove geographic, sanctions, consumer-protection, or product restrictions. When an approval is absent, the implementation stops at a sandbox demonstration rather than sending live transactions through an unrelated merchant account.

Expose the economics without confusing client payment volume with agency revenue. On $1,000,000 monthly merchant volume, a simplified 2.10% wholesale cost is $21,000. Merchant pricing of 5.50% produces $55,000 in charges and a $34,000 gross spread; 8.90% produces $89,000 and a $68,000 gross spread. These are payment-operator figures before additional network charges, refunds, losses, operating expenses, and contractual allocations, not this agency's recognized implementation revenue. A 10% rolling reserve withholds $100,000 of that month's eligible volume under the assumed reserve basis. Reserve balances remain restricted merchant funds or associated settlement obligations according to the actual arrangement, never free agency income. The agency instead might invoice a $25,000 deployment and $5,000 monthly support, already counted within the chapter's canonical revenue mixes. Build a merchant-level settlement ledger that distinguishes captured principal, processor fees, refunds, reserves, releases, and actual agency invoices. Reconcile provider statements against transaction identifiers daily. An unexplained difference triggers investigation and client notification, not an automatic balancing entry that hides the discrepancy or inflates reported service revenue.

Make payment routing deterministic and bounded. Tokenize card details through the authorized gateway; the agency workflow stores tokens and minimal transaction metadata, not raw card data in prompts or general logs. A decline classifier follows processor guidance: hard declines stop, while eligible soft declines receive only explicitly permitted retries on approved routes. Cascading must never disguise the merchant, evade issuer decisions, or send duplicate authorizations after a timeout without checking transaction status. For this mapped offer, require a documented 10% rolling reserve arrangement before enabling live routing, and enforce the contracted release schedule. Configure Verifi RDR pre-dispute refunds with merchant authorization, financial thresholds, and reconciliation; refund automation does not erase dispute obligations. Use supported 3DS2 step-up authentication for designated high-risk BIN and transaction cohorts, alongside broader fraud signals, and maintain recognizable merchant descriptors. Humans handle merchant onboarding, route changes, exceptional refunds, and consequential risk decisions. For covered recurring consumer electronic fund transfers, implement authorization and copy requirements under 12 CFR 1005.10(b); for covered online negative-option offers, address 15 U.S.C. 8403. Provider outages fall back to a pending state or controlled stop, never blind multi-bank retries.

sections.heading: 4. Compound distribution while controlling run cost, review load, and owner profit
paragraphs: Price automation from accepted work, not token invoices alone. Assume one model-assisted run uses 2,000 input tokens priced at $2.40 per million and 400 output tokens priced at $8.00 per million. These illustrative rates produce $0.0048 input cost and $0.0032 output cost. Add $0.002 orchestration, $0.005 evidence retrieval, and $0.005 storage and telemetry for $0.02 machine cost per attempted run. At 10,000 runs, machine spend is $200. Reviewing 200 sampled runs for two minutes each at $60 hourly costs $400; handling 50 additional exception runs for six minutes each costs $300. With $300 allocated platform overhead, total cost is $1,200, or $0.12 per attempted run. If only 9,500 runs meet acceptance criteria, cost per accepted run is approximately $0.1263. These review volumes illustrate low-consequence work only; consequential outputs require their designated human review even if that changes the economics. Set tenant spend limits, maximum retries, evidence-size limits, and review-queue capacity before increasing traffic. A cheaper model that doubles exception handling can be more expensive than a stronger model with stable structured outputs.

Connect distribution to verified delivery artifacts. Publish programmatic pages only when each page contains useful connector-specific material: supported fields, setup steps, measured failure modes, and a real acceptance checklist. Use Google Search Console to track qualified organic visits, not just indexed URLs. Offer an optional shareable, redacted workflow health report that clients can forward to a peer; obtain permission before publishing any client name, metric, or configuration. For outbound, combine licensed business-contact data with a relevant diagnostic and honor suppression lists under 15 U.S.C. 7704. Avoid fake personalization or unsupported savings claims, which create risk under 15 U.S.C. 45. A planning funnel of 1,000 carefully selected monthly contacts, 4% positive responses, 50% meeting conversion, 40% proposal conversion, and 25% close conversion produces two expected wins, not two booked contracts. Record cohort dates and actual conversion counts in HubSpot, then reconcile won deals to delivery capacity. With $4,000 monthly acquisition spending, two wins imply $2,000 cash acquisition cost per win before unallocated labor. Do not annualize this funnel into the canonical scenarios; pause campaigns when support queues or implementation backlogs exceed the team's service commitments.

Reconcile the operating plan to the scorecard every month. Conservative revenue can comprise four $15,000 sprints plus two retainers billed for ten months at $2,000 monthly: $60,000 plus $40,000 equals $100,000. Its $80,000 total expense envelope leaves $20,000 owner net profit at 20%. Base uses ten $25,000 sprints and five twelve-month $5,000 retainers: $250,000 plus $300,000 equals $550,000; $385,000 total expenses leave $165,000 at 30.0%. Scaled uses sixteen $25,000 sprints and ten twelve-month $5,000 retainers: $400,000 plus $600,000 equals $1,000,000; $600,000 total expenses leave $400,000 at 40%. Conservative and Base retain 2 FT + 3 C; Scaled uses 3 FT + 4 C. These rosters are canonical staffing assumptions, not evidence that local full-year compensation fits every expense envelope; validate paid hours, owner compensation treatment, and contractor utilization before committing. Count marketplace and payment examples within these totals rather than adding them again. Release new workflow versions through replay tests, shadow execution, and bounded live cohorts. Roll back model and prompt versions together, reconcile destination side effects, and replay only jobs whose idempotency protections survive the incident.

chapters.question_prompt: How do you structure a lean 2 FT + 3 C (5 people) -> 3 FT + 4 C (7 people) pod, enforce weekly scorecards, and build transferable books that command a premium exit multiple (or durable cash cow)?
chapters.title: Pod Architecture, Contractor KPIs & Exit Valuation
chapters.subtitle: Five-to-Seven-Person Delivery Pods, Weekly Acceptance Economics, Accrual Cohorts, Signed IP Transfers, and Buyer-Tested Earnings
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #29, Productized AI Agencies, holds Rank #06 with an 86/100 Money-to-Manpower Score across 23 mapped plays. The operating asset is a repeatable delivery pod, not the founder's ability to rescue every deployment. Assign five seats across scope control, architecture, implementation, independent QA, and monitoring; expand to seven only against funded backlog and measured capacity. Canonical annual owner profit is $20,000 Conservative, $165,000 Base, and $400,000 Scaled. Preserve those cases through acceptance-linked contractor payments, customer and counterparty exposure limits of 25%, accrual books, signed IP assignments, and documented access authority. Weekly evidence must connect delivered work to recognized fees and support obligations. A buyer pays for transferable earnings; a continuing owner collects the same discipline as durable cash.

sections.heading: 1. Give every play one accountable seat and a funded capacity envelope
paragraphs: Build Candidate #29 around two employee seats and three bounded contractor work packages. FT1 owns commercial qualification, scope, pricing, collections, and customer relationships; FT2 owns architecture, technical acceptance, access authorization, and production accountability. C1 implements approved integrations, C2 independently tests outputs and security boundaries, and C3 maintains monitoring, runbooks, and scheduled support coverage. Contractors are not three additional unlimited employees hidden inside a retainer. Maintain the existing 23-play register with its authoritative identifiers, then allocate primary accountability across these seats: four plays to FT1, six to FT2, five to C1, four to C2, and four to C3. This is a work-allocation model, not a replacement taxonomy for the mapped plays. Every register entry needs one accountable owner, one backup, an acceptance artifact, a client-data boundary, and an estimated monthly load. Keep sales promises, implementation work, and final acceptance visibly separate even when a small team shares meetings. FT2 may reject C1's delivery without renegotiating commercial scope; FT1 may sell an extension only after capacity and pricing are recalculated. Store the register in Linear or Jira and attach versioned evidence in the agency's authorized GitHub organization.

Size work from available delivery hours rather than impressive headcount. As an explicit planning example, reserve 40 weekly hours across the two full-time seats for delivery after sales, administration, and leadership, and contract another 45 hours of specialist capacity. At 70% planned utilization, that creates 59.5 scheduled delivery hours while preserving 25.5 hours for variance, investigation, and interruptions. A sprint requiring 45 delivery hours consumes roughly three quarters of that weekly envelope; two simultaneous starts would exceed it. Measure actual effort for four weeks before raising concurrency. The Conservative scorecard's $100,000 revenue and $20,000 owner profit leave only $80,000 for total annual costs. That amount generally cannot sustain two market-paid full-time employees, three contractors, and operating overhead. Preserve the canonical 2 FT + 3 C label, but flag its staffing feasibility instead of silently treating employees as fractional. Owner compensation, local wage requirements, payroll burden, and startup funding need an explicit reconciliation. Funding supplies cash, not profit, and founder labor still has a replacement cost. Do not launch a payroll commitment until actual contracts and available capital cover the resulting obligations.

Expand to 3 FT + 4 C by adding FT3 as delivery manager and customer-success owner, plus C4 as a second implementation specialist with recovery capability. Transfer four existing play accountabilities to FT3 and two to C4; rebalance the original seats so the register still totals exactly 23, rather than manufacturing new plays to justify hiring. The third employee should remove founder coordination and renewal dependence before adding another technical bottleneck. Require eight weeks of signed, contribution-positive backlog, demonstrated support demand, and a cash forecast that survives the largest customer paying thirty days late. These are internal planning thresholds, not claims about every agency's demand cycle. Use named backups for each privileged system, but never shared credentials; maintain individual accounts, least-privilege roles, and documented emergency access. Contractor classification depends on actual working conditions, not the label in a statement of work. Assess applicable wage, tax, and state tests, including California Labor Code section 2775 where relevant. Specify deliverables and service windows without assuming that compulsory employee-like schedules become independent contracting merely because invoices arrive through Deel or another payment platform.

sections.heading: 2. Pay for accepted work and run one evidence-backed weekly scorecard
paragraphs: Contract compensation should make quality observable without forcing specialists to absorb unlimited client ambiguity. An illustrative $6,000 integration package can pay $1,200 after approved design, $3,600 after independently verified staging acceptance, and $1,200 after production handoff with a complete runbook. Define invoice dates, review deadlines, written rejection reasons, and dispute handling; pay undisputed amounts when due under the agreement and applicable law. Price scope changes separately rather than withholding earned fees to obtain extra features. Establish a five-business-day acceptance review window and a thirty-day correction period for reproducible defects against the frozen specification. New model behavior, upstream API changes, and customer process changes require triage before anyone assigns responsibility. Keep QA compensation independent of the number of releases approved, and never reward a reviewer for hiding defects to accelerate collections. As a sprint illustration, a $15,000 implementation fee less $6,000 implementation, $1,200 independent QA, $300 attributable usage, and $1,500 allocated employee delivery cost produces $6,000 delivery contribution, or 40%. That contribution still must cover selling, administration, support obligations, and other overhead before it becomes owner profit.

Publish Friday's scorecard from source systems, not a manually polished slide. Linear supplies accepted milestones and cycle times; GitHub supplies reviewed changes; Harvest supplies effort; the accounting ledger supplies accrued revenue and costs; authorized monitoring supplies usage and incident events. Track first-pass acceptance as accepted first submissions divided by all first submissions, with the sample count beside the rate. Use an initial 90% target, but investigate small samples rather than ranking contractors on one unusual ticket. Track rework hours divided by total delivery hours, targeting below 10%, and on-time milestones divided by milestones due, targeting at least 95%. Define a blocker before measuring it and report its age and accountable decision maker. Pair automation completion with error severity, human override rate, and the proportion of consequential decisions reviewed by an authorized person. A faster workflow that silently sends inaccurate customer communications is not a quality improvement. Review contribution by project, retainer consumption, overdue receivables, and committed capacity in the same meeting. Each adverse signal gets one owner, one corrective action, and a dated evidence requirement rather than another status discussion.

Write service levels around coverage the pod can actually supply. An illustrative managed retainer can include weekday coverage from 09:00 to 17:00 in the named client timezone, one-business-hour acknowledgement for a production blocker, and four-covered-hour acknowledgement for degraded service. Acknowledgement is not restoration. Define containment, customer updates, escalation, and recovery objectives separately; do not promise continuous response from three part-time contractor packages. For an exposed data path or unauthorized action, empower the designated responder to disable the affected automation, preserve necessary evidence, and notify FT2 immediately through the documented channel. Applicable customer contracts and incident laws determine external notification duties. Test the fallback with synthetic records, including expired credentials, model timeouts, duplicate webhook delivery, and malformed structured outputs. Use idempotency keys and transaction boundaries where supported instead of assuming a retry is harmless. The Monday review approves only the corrective work that fits purchased capacity and records whether a client change order is required. Persistent misses trigger narrower scope, additional purchased coverage, or a replacement supplier after an orderly handoff, not concealed unpaid overtime or optimistic changes to the scorecard definitions.

sections.heading: 3. Reconcile accrual books, cohort retention, and concentrated exposures
paragraphs: Keep implementation revenue, managed support revenue, client business outcomes, and cash receipts in separate fields. Candidate #29 earns fees and retainers; a client's increased sales, reduced payroll effort, or processed transaction value is not agency revenue. The canonical annual bridges are exact: Conservative revenue of $100,000 less $80,000 total costs equals $20,000 owner profit; Base revenue of $550,000 less $385,000 equals $165,000; Scaled revenue of $1,000,000 less $600,000 equals $400,000. Those are respectively 20%, 30.0%, and 40% net margins, not delivery contribution percentages. Do not turn the $2,500-$18,000 monthly operating-expense planning range into a substitute for complete annual costs; document which direct labor and other costs sit outside that narrower budget. An illustrative Base revenue bridge is twenty $15,000 implementations plus ten accounts averaging $25,000 recognized annual support fees. A Scaled bridge is twenty-five $20,000 implementations plus twenty accounts averaging $25,000 support fees. Both reconcile exactly, but neither demonstrates delivery feasibility until hours and service obligations fit the relevant pod. Conservative could comprise four $15,000 implementations and four $10,000 annual support accounts, subject to the staffing cost constraint already identified.

Use accrual schedules that explain when services are earned, not merely when Stripe pays the bank. For a $24,000 annual stand-ready support arrangement collected in advance, recognizing $2,000 monthly is appropriate only when the service obligation is satisfied evenly through that period. Record the unearned balance as a contract liability. Implementation recognition depends on the contractual performance obligations and the applicable accounting framework; a deposit or invoice milestone alone does not establish that delivery has occurred. Have the accountant document that policy and apply it consistently. Accrue accepted contractor work before the invoice arrives, allocate attributable model and hosting usage, and reconcile bank, receivable, payable, and contract-liability balances monthly. Maintain customer cohorts by first support-service month, recording starting recurring fees, expansion, contraction, churn, contribution, and support hours. Gross revenue retention excludes expansion; net revenue retention includes it, while both exclude new customers from the starting cohort. Report implementation fees separately so a large sprint cannot disguise shrinking recurring support. Preserve signed scope changes and credit notes alongside the ledger entries so a buyer can reproduce both revenue timing and delivery economics.

Set a maximum 25% customer concentration policy against trailing-twelve-month recognized revenue, forward contracted fees, and gross receivables, testing each denominator separately. Aggregate entities under common control; five subsidiaries of one sponsor do not create five independent revenue risks. At Base revenue, the trailing annual customer limit is $137,500; at Scaled it is $250,000; at Conservative it is $25,000. During startup, the first customer necessarily breaches a diversified revenue limit. Record that exception with a dated diversification plan, and restrict new fixed commitments until exposure falls within policy. Apply the same 25% maximum to material reseller or referral counterparties using attributable recognized fees. For critical delivery suppliers, measure non-substitutable delivery exposure rather than pretending low invoice spend means low dependency. A sole model provider may support every workflow despite costing little; tested fallbacks reduce this exposure only when authorized and operational. Track contractor replacement time and cash held with payment intermediaries separately. A cap does not repair a breach automatically: require an owner, an exposure-reduction action, and evidence that the alternative works before describing the book as diversified.

sections.heading: 4. Build transferable earnings before negotiating an exit multiple
paragraphs: Transferability begins with ownership and permissions, not a broker presentation. Under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a), a copyright ownership transfer generally requires a signed writing from the owner or authorized agent. Obtain signed contractor assignments covering commissioned code, prompts where protectable, documentation, tests, and other protectable deliverables; do not rely exclusively on a work-made-for-hire label for contractor software. Separate preexisting tools, third-party components, and client-owned materials in schedules with the actual licenses needed for continued operation and transfer. A contractor cannot assign rights they never owned, and an agency cannot promise exclusive ownership of every machine-generated output. Document customer access authority, processing instructions, subprocessors, retention limits, and deletion procedures. California service-provider arrangements, where applicable, require contract terms and practices consistent with Civil Code section 1798.100(d) and relevant implementing rules. Review customer assignment and change-of-control clauses before modeling a sale. Maintain human review for consequential decisions and retain evidence supporting performance claims under the FTC Act's prohibition on deceptive practices. These records protect ongoing delivery and let a buyer identify rights they can actually acquire.

Use valuation multiples as negotiation sensitivities, not as automatic rewards for mentioning AI. An illustrative owner-operated agency might be tested at 2.0-3.0 times normalized seller's discretionary earnings, while a manager-run agency with durable retention and transferable contracts might be tested at 3.0-5.0 times normalized EBITDA. These are planning ranges, not observed transaction comparables. Actual bids depend on scale, customer quality, growth, market conditions, and deal structure. The canonical $165,000 Base owner profit is neither automatically SDE nor EBITDA. Build a bridge showing owner wages already expensed, genuine discretionary costs, interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization, and required replacement management. If that bridge independently supports $165,000 SDE, the illustrative 2.0-3.0 range implies $330,000-$495,000 enterprise value. If a separately verified Scaled bridge supports $300,000 normalized EBITDA after replacement management, 3.0-5.0 implies $900,000-$1,500,000 enterprise value. The $300,000 example is an assumed valuation input, not a revision to the $400,000 canonical owner profit. Never combine an SDE add-back with an EBITDA multiple while omitting the employee needed to replace the departing owner.

Prepare a buyer room that reconciles monthly ledgers to contracts, cohort retention, bank activity, delivery evidence, and the 23-play register. Include the weekly scorecards, contractor agreements, signed IP chain, customer transfer restrictions, security incidents, recovery tests, and a schedule of unfulfilled prepaid services. Share redacted summaries first; disclose customer data only through authorized, necessary diligence access with controlled recipients and an access log. Run a four-week founder-absence exercise in which the pod handles renewals, deployment decisions, and incident triage without undocumented intervention. Measure delivery misses and replacement labor rather than declaring independence because the founder stopped attending standups. Enterprise value does not equal cash received: reconcile debt, cash treatment, normalized working capital, transaction costs, holdbacks, and contingent consideration separately. Prepaid support liabilities need explicit treatment so the seller cannot retain all collections while leaving unfunded service obligations behind. If bids undervalue durable earnings, retain the business with the same concentration limits and management coverage. Distributions should follow payroll, tax obligations, service reserves, and the cash forecast; recurring owner profit is valuable only when operations can keep producing it.

callout.title: Verify the book before presenting premium valuation claims
callout.body: Use four pre-flight checks before expanding the pod or circulating a buyer earnings package; retain unresolved exceptions in the record.
items: Reconcile all three canonical cases exactly, and identify whether each proposed earnings multiple uses verified SDE or normalized EBITDA.
Confirm that all 23 mapped plays have named owners, tested backups, acceptance evidence, and capacity within the five-person or seven-person roster.
Verify signed IP transfers, customer-system authorization, processing terms, third-party licenses, and contract transfer requirements before sharing diligence materials.
Test customer and counterparty concentrations against the 25% limits, and document working fallbacks or dated remediation for every exception.

chapters.pull_quote: A transferable agency sells evidence-backed earnings, not the founder's willingness to remain indispensable.
action_checklist: Assign the existing 23 mapped plays across FT1, FT2, C1, C2, and C3 with one accountable owner, backup, acceptance artifact, and measured capacity estimate each.
Price contractor packages with staged acceptance payments, independent QA, explicit correction boundaries, and service windows the pod can actually staff.
Publish a weekly source-linked scorecard covering acceptance, rework, delivery timeliness, contribution, support consumption, incident response, and corrective-action ownership.
Close monthly accrual books to the canonical revenue and owner-profit bridges, separating client business outcomes, deposits, earned fees, contractor accruals, and service liabilities.
Enforce customer and counterparty exposure limits of 25%, aggregate common-control entities, and record startup or supplier exceptions with tested reduction plans.
Complete signed IP assignments, contract-transfer review, a four-week founder-absence test, and separate SDE and EBITDA bridges before evaluating sale proceeds or continued distributions.

statutory_citations.relevance: Copyright ownership transfers generally require a signed writing from the rights owner or authorized agent; maintain an auditable contractor assignment chain for protectable agency deliverables.

statutory_citations.title: 17 U.S.C. section 101 — Definitions, including work made for hire
statutory_citations.relevance: Commissioned works satisfy the statutory work-made-for-hire definition only under specified conditions; contractor software should not rely on that label as a substitute for appropriate signed assignments.

statutory_citations.title: California Labor Code section 2775 — Worker classification framework
statutory_citations.relevance: Evaluate applicable worker-classification requirements and statutory exceptions using actual operating facts before treating recurring delivery seats as independent contractors.

statutory_citations.title: California Civil Code section 1798.100(d) — Personal-information contract requirements
statutory_citations.relevance: For covered arrangements, contracts governing disclosures to service providers, contractors, or third parties must include required purposes, protections, oversight rights, and remediation provisions.

statutory_citations.title: 15 U.S.C. section 45(a) — Unfair or deceptive acts or practices
statutory_citations.relevance: Keep evidence supporting AI performance, savings, reliability, and service claims; misleading claims can create exposure under the FTC Act's prohibition on unfair or deceptive practices.

statutory_citations.title: 29 U.S.C. sections 206 and 207 — Minimum wage and overtime requirements
statutory_citations.relevance: Budget applicable wage and overtime obligations for covered employees; contract labels and optimistic unit economics do not remove statutory pay requirements, and state requirements may be more protective.

chapters.question_prompt: What is the exact Day-1-to-Day-30 execution schedule for launching productized ai agencies, and what quantitative thresholds govern Kill, Fix, or Scale decisions at Day 30/60/90?
chapters.title: The First 30-Day Launch Sprint & Kill / Fix / Scale Gates
chapters.subtitle: A Five-Person Sprint for Fixed-Scope AI Implementations: Authorized Access, Paid Pilots, Evaluation Evidence, and Day-30/60/90 Cash Decisions
chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #29, Productized AI Agencies, holds Rank #06 with an 86/100 Money-to-Manpower Score and 23 mapped plays. Launch through one narrow workflow, one paid implementation offer, and one measurable acceptance contract rather than a catalog of custom agents. This sprint assigns commercial and technical ownership across two full-time operators and three contractors, caps initial cash exposure at $7,500, and converts daily evidence into explicit Day-30/60/90 decisions. The canonical annual owner-profit cases remain $20,000 Conservative, $165,000 Base, and $400,000 Scaled; client savings never become agency revenue. Scale requires paid demand, repeatable delivery, safe exception handling, and positive project economics. Fix weak evidence with a bounded experiment; kill an exhausted offer rather than financing indefinite customization.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Sell One Authorized Workflow Before Building a Platform
paragraphs: Start with a single operational buyer and an observable queue: for example, a B2B distributor whose service team manually classifies inbound order-status requests. Sell classification, retrieval from approved order records, and a draft response for staff review; exclude payment changes, credit decisions, and unattended customer messages. The offer is a fixed-scope implementation, not ownership of the client's entire AI roadmap. Assign the first full-time operator to interviews, proposals, collections, and account decisions. Assign the second to architecture, integration, release control, and technical support. The three contractors cover workflow integration, independent evaluation, and security or data-contract review under explicit hour limits. These are specialist roles, not three additional full-time delivery seats. Candidate #29's 23 mapped plays belong in a coverage ledger with an owner, evidence link, estimated hours, and current disposition. Use the 23 local execution slots below to organize that ledger; they are working assignments, not claimed source titles for the mapped plays. Preserve original play identifiers when transferring the ledger into the broader manuscript or operating system. This prevents a large play catalog from becoming an accidental promise to deliver 23 separate services during the launch month.

Days 1 through 3 establish the commercial boundary before production access. P01 is buyer selection, P02 is workflow baseline, and P03 is the fixed-scope offer. Require a buyer to identify weekly ticket volume, current handling time, responsible staff, and the consequence of a wrong answer. Measure a sample of at least 30 historical tickets with timestamps rather than accepting an executive's rough savings estimate. A buyer reporting 500 monthly tickets at eight minutes each has approximately 66.7 monthly handling hours; reducing that workload does not create 66.7 hours of agency revenue. State the deliverable as one queue, two approved connectors, one escalation destination, and a defined evaluation set. Price the initial illustrative pilot at $7,500, with $3,750 due at signing and $3,750 after documented acceptance. Specify what happens when client credentials or representative examples arrive late: the delivery clock pauses rather than silently consuming the pod's capacity. Define change requests by connector count, output type, and exception category. A new CRM, another language, or automatic sending becomes a separately estimated change, not an informal favor absorbed by the technical operator.

Days 4 through 7 complete P04 access authorization, P05 data and IP terms, and P06 qualification. Obtain written permission from the client resource owner identifying systems, environments, permitted operations, and access expiry. Use a dedicated HubSpot sandbox or Microsoft 365 test mailbox where available; never ask a salesperson to share their personal administrator password. Computer access outside authorization can implicate 18 U.S.C. § 1030(a)(2)(C), so record the actual authorization boundary rather than treating possession of a token as permission. Contract language should distinguish client inputs, agency reusable components, third-party dependencies, and commissioned deliverables. An intended copyright ownership transfer requires a signed writing under 17 U.S.C. § 204(a). For covered California personal information, evaluate the applicable service-provider or contractor terms under California Civil Code § 1798.100(d). Build the first 60-account prospect list around one workflow and buying role. Target 12 completed discovery meetings by Day 30, but do not equate outreach activity with validated demand. Each meeting must record urgency, an accountable budget holder, accessible source data, and an agreed next action before it enters the qualified pipeline.

sections.heading: 2. Days 8–14: Build the Smallest Measurable Implementation
paragraphs: Week two turns buyer evidence into six more local execution slots: P07 process mapping, P08 connector design, P09 reference implementation, P10 evaluation construction, P11 exception routing, and P12 proposal closure. Map the present workflow before inserting a model: intake, identity lookup, record retrieval, draft generation, staff review, and final disposition. Use n8n or a small Python service when those tools fit the client's environment; select one orchestration path instead of supporting both during the pilot. Keep deterministic rules outside the model: allowed account IDs, field permissions, retry counts, and destination addresses belong in ordinary code. The model should return a constrained classification and structured draft, not executable instructions. Treat incoming email text and retrieved documents as untrusted content. A message telling the agent to reveal credentials must remain data, even when it resembles an internal instruction. Store credentials in the client's approved secret manager, separate development and production identities, and record connector permissions in the deployment manifest. On Day 10, demonstrate a synthetic ticket flowing through the entire route, including an intentional failure that lands in the human queue without sending a customer message.

Build a frozen acceptance set of at least 100 representative cases for each workflow before tuning prompts against it. Reserve those cases from development examples, label the expected routing and factual requirements, and include ambiguous requests, missing records, duplicate events, hostile instructions, and cross-account lookup attempts. The launch threshold is at least 95 passing cases out of 100, zero critical data-boundary or unauthorized-action failures, and human review of every consequential decision. A case passes only when all mandatory checks pass; averaging a correct classification with an invented order status hides a real defect. Record the model identifier, prompt version, connector version, source-record timestamp, latency, and measured cost with every evaluation run. Use pytest for deterministic assertions and an independent contractor's rubric for response quality. An automated grader can triage cases but cannot certify its own unsupported answers. Repeat the acceptance suite after any model, prompt, retrieval, or permissions change. These results support a narrow claim about tested conditions, not universal reliability. Under Section 5 of the FTC Act, 15 U.S.C. § 45, performance claims must avoid deceptive representations; maintain the evidence supporting each published number.

The commercial operator continues discovery while the technical operator protects build capacity. Submit four qualified proposals by Day 30, each with the same scope boundary and a buyer-specific baseline attachment. Do not discount away uncertainty: offer paid discovery when connector feasibility remains unresolved, and count that as discovery revenue rather than a completed implementation. For the $7,500 pilot, budget 45 direct delivery hours at an illustrative loaded rate of $80, $300 of runtime and tooling, and $350 of warranty allowance. Total direct cost is $4,250; project contribution is $3,250, or approximately 43.3%. This is contribution before shared overhead, selling costs, and the full owner-profit calculation. Track both operators' delivery time even when they defer cash compensation. A pilot apparently producing 70% contribution because founder hours are missing is a pricing error. On Day 14, require a working demonstration, versioned evaluation results, and either a signed funded pilot or a documented next buying event. The scorecard's one-to-four-month first-deal window means an unsigned proposal at two weeks is evidence to manage, not automatic proof that the opportunity has failed.

callout.body: The best launch shortcuts reduce uncertainty without hiding delivery cost or transferring an uncontrolled failure to the client.
items: Capture connector setup as a reusable checklist, but keep credentials and client-specific identifiers outside the reusable package.
Include deliberate missing-record cases in the sales demonstration; a clean human handoff often sells reliability better than a polished best-case answer.

sections.heading: 3. Days 15–21: Deliver Evidence Within a Measured Cash and Capacity Envelope
paragraphs: Week three covers P13 deployment preparation, P14 staged release, P15 usage monitoring, P16 quality monitoring, P17 acceptance, and P18 support packaging. Begin with read-only access and staff-visible drafts. Enable writes only when the contract expressly includes them, the resource owner authorizes them, and idempotency tests show retries cannot create duplicate actions. Use a unique event key and durable processing record rather than trusting a webhook provider to deliver each message once. Log request IDs, status transitions, costs, and error categories while excluding unnecessary message content. Configure Sentry or the client's existing observability stack to alert on repeated connector failures and dead-letter queue growth. On Day 18, reconcile production samples against the frozen rubric, then investigate discrepancies between test and live traffic. On Day 19, demonstrate credential revocation and restoration of the original human workflow. Acceptance requires the client's named reviewer to confirm scope completion and unresolved exceptions in writing. A successful internal demo is not client acceptance, and an issued invoice is not collected cash. These distinctions keep the sprint board honest when technical progress moves faster than procurement, customer review, or payment processing.

Set the first-month gross cash-spend ceiling at $7,500 before committing contractor work. Allocate $2,500 to overhead, $2,500 to specialist payments, $750 to software and API usage, $750 to acquisition activity, and $1,000 to contingency. These envelopes sum exactly to the ceiling; using the contingency requires removing the amount from its remaining balance. Maintain a separate accrued-cost ledger because deferred operator compensation does not disappear economically. For planning, add a $5,000 founder-labor charge if that labor is unpaid during launch, producing $12,500 of modeled first-month cost before any further accruals. Do not add that charge twice when allocating delivery labor into project contribution. Cap the two full-time operators at 240 combined planned hours for the month: 160 for delivery and 80 for sales, administration, and support. Cap contractor usage at 60 combined hours, with actual rates reconciled to the $2,500 envelope before booking. If specialist rates consume the cash allowance earlier, cash controls the limit. Reserve at least 40 delivery hours for defects and handover. Run one live implementation at a time during launch rather than converting theoretical hours into overlapping customer promises.

Keep sprint economics separate from the canonical annual scenarios. Conservative remains $100,000 revenue less $80,000 total costs, producing $20,000 owner net profit at 20% margin with 2 FT + 3 C. Base remains $550,000 less $385,000, producing $165,000 at 30.0% with the same pod. Scaled remains $1,000,000 less $600,000, producing $400,000 at 40% with 3 FT + 4 C. Illustrative revenue bridges are eight $7,500 implementations plus forty $1,000 support-months; forty $10,000 implementations plus one hundred $1,500 support-months; and sixty $12,500 implementations plus one hundred twenty-five $2,000 support-months, respectively. These equal the three revenue totals but do not establish that launch capacity can deliver them. The Base bridge requires material reuse and shorter implementation cycles before forty annual projects fit. Support-months count active billable months, not distinct clients or unearned annual contract value. The published $2,500–$18,000 monthly opex range is not a substitute for each scenario's total annual costs. Include delivery labor, contractors, acquisition, support, and other operating expenses in the reconciliation. None of the bridges recognizes client sales, order value, or estimated labor savings as agency revenue.

sections.heading: 4. Days 22–30: Close the Evidence Ledger and Apply Kill, Fix, or Scale
paragraphs: Week four completes P19 incident rehearsal, P20 economic reconciliation, P21 proof packaging, P22 renewal and referral development, and P23 portfolio decisions. Day 22 runs an incident exercise covering leaked credentials, wrong-account retrieval, and an unavailable connector. Day 23 reconciles recorded hours, runtime charges, warranty usage, invoices, and collections. Day 24 prepares a case study limited to measured results and obtains explicit permission before publishing client identifiers or operational details. Day 25 presents a bounded support retainer and asks for a referral only after acceptance. Day 26 reviews all 23 ledger slots, distinguishing completed evidence from deferred work. Day 27 has the independent tester challenge the latest release with new adversarial cases without replacing the frozen acceptance benchmark. Day 28 refreshes the cash forecast and remaining delivery commitments. Day 29 writes a one-page decision memo with raw denominators, failed criteria, and one recommended action. Day 30 is the decision meeting, not a ceremonial launch announcement. Both full-time operators sign the memo, assign the next experiment or capacity increase, and preserve the underlying evidence. Contractors contribute their findings but do not create open-ended work commitments for the next month.

Apply the decision matrix in order: any applicable Kill condition overrides Scale; Scale requires every listed commercial condition plus the common delivery controls; all remaining cases are Fix. Kill normally means stop selling the tested offer or segment, not delete customer records or abandon contracted support. A critical security failure triggers immediate suspension of the affected workflow regardless of meeting date; resume only after remediation and independent retesting. Common Scale controls are at least 95% passing cases on each workflow's minimum 100-case acceptance set, zero unresolved critical failures, at least 40% aggregate implementation contribution, rework no greater than 10% of direct delivery hours, and at least 90% on-time accepted deliveries. With fewer than ten deliveries, require every delivery on time. Count rework as correcting defective agreed functionality, not separately purchased changes. Require collection of at least 95% of amounts currently due, no overdue critical incident, and no pilot above 45 direct delivery hours. Treat these thresholds as operating choices, not scorecard-derived promises. In particular, Day-30 Scale is an ambitious evidence threshold within a business whose first deal may reasonably take four months.

Keep cumulative gross spending within $7,500 by Day 30, $20,000 by Day 60, and $35,000 by Day 90, while limiting cumulative unrecovered launch cash to $7,500 throughout. Calculate unrecovered cash as cumulative cash outflows minus cumulative client collections; protect tax reserves and any refundable balances separately. Additional spending after Day 30 must fit both the gross ceiling and that net-exposure limit, so optimistic receivables cannot fund hiring. A Fix decision authorizes one fourteen-day experiment with a named owner, a single variable, and at most $1,500 inside the existing ceilings. Test a narrower buyer, simpler connector, revised price, or stronger exception route; do not change everything simultaneously. Scale first means repeating the accepted package, not adding employees. Increase concurrent implementations from one to two only after three consecutive accepted projects meet the common controls and planned utilization stays below 75% of available delivery hours. A $1,500 monthly retainer with $600 direct service cost contributes $900 before overhead; reserve those service hours before selling another sprint. Move toward the canonical 3 FT + 4 C scaled team only when contracted work and collected cash support the added capacity.
